reports.title: Reports
reports.subtitle: Browse and track issues reported across the city.
reports.pageOf: Page {page, number} of {pages, number} · {total, number} total

hero.body: Residents report local problems (potholes, broken lights, garbage, flooding) with a photo and map location, then follow them from submission to resolution.
hero.artLabel: Animated map with a pulsing location pin

how.title: From report to resolution in three steps

report.title: Report
report.body: Describe the issue, add a photo, and drop a pin on the map.

verify.title: Verify
verify.body: Neighbours confirm it and admins review and assign it to a department.

resolve.title: Resolve
resolve.body: Track status changes and get notified when it’s fixed.

features.title: Everything a report needs to get fixed

pin.title: Pin the exact spot
pin.body: Drop a marker on the map, and every report carries precise GPS coordinates.

photo.title: Photo evidence
photo.body: Attach a picture so the problem is unmistakable. Image type is verified on the server.

community.title: Community verification
community.body: Neighbours upvote and confirm reports, surfacing what matters most.

tracking.title: Transparent tracking
tracking.body: Follow each report through a clear six-stage lifecycle, from submission to fix.

routing.title: Routed to the right team
routing.body: Admins assign each issue to the department responsible for resolving it.

notify.title: Stay in the loop
notify.body: Get notified the moment your report changes status or gets resolved.

audiences.title: For the people who report, and the people who fix

items.report: Report an issue in under a minute
items.map: See what others have flagged nearby on the map
items.confirm: Confirm and upvote to add weight to a report
items.track: Track progress and get notified on every change

items.assign: Assign work to the responsible department
items.workflow: Move issues through the status workflow
items.trends: Monitor trends on the analytics dashboard

cta.title: Spotted something broken? Report it.
cta.body: It takes about a minute, and your neighbours can back you up. Every report is public and tracked to resolution.

map.title: Map
map.subtitle: Every reported issue, plotted by location. Shaded areas are hotspots, where reports cluster.

map.cameBack: A fixed problem came back here.

hotspots.heading: Hotspots
hotspots.intro: Places with at least {min, number} reports within {radius, number} m of each other in the last {days, number} days, fixed ones included. Most reports first.
hotspots.none: No hotspots right now: no place has {min, number} or more reports this close together.
hotspots.kindsMore: {top} and {others, plural, one {# other kind} other {# other kinds}}

scorecards.title: Department scorecards
scorecards.subtitle: How quickly each department responds to and resolves the reports assigned to it.
scorecards.none: Scorecards appear here once departments are set up.
scorecards.statement: {count, plural, =0 {No report is past its resolution target right now.} one {# report is past its resolution target right now.} other {# reports are past their resolution target right now.}}
scorecards.cutShort: Showing the {shown, number} most overdue of {total, number}.

notes.clock: The clock starts when a report is assigned to a department, so time waiting for review does not count against it. A reassigned report counts for its current department.
notes.firstResponse: First response is the department's first status change after assignment.
notes.window: Scores cover reports assigned in the last {days, number} days. A report still within its target counts neither way. Overdue reports are counted whatever their age.
notes.excluded: Reports rejected or marked as duplicates had nothing to resolve, so they are left out of the resolved percentages.
notes.disputed: A fix that residents dispute with photos goes back to the department, and the report counts as unresolved again.
notes.median: Typical means the median: half of reports were faster, half slower.
